question: Which properties of the training data (format, sampling, intermediate steps, text mixing) and of the model (scale, pretraining, tokenizer) make small transformers learn arithmetic efficiently with the plain next-token objective?
hypothesis: Plain MSB-first addition is hard for next-token prediction because the first output digit depends on all input digits; reversing the output or adding chain-of-thought intermediate steps makes the function easier and cuts sample complexity.
contributions: Data format and sampling matter: reversed output and balanced digit/carry sampling improve learning, with sharp phase transitions explained via low-rank matrix completion
Chain-of-thought (scratchpad) training data improves accuracy, sample complexity and convergence even without pretraining
Study of text/arithmetic mixing, few-shot prompting, pretraining, tokenization and model scale (NanoGPT, GPT-2, GPT-3)
Length generalization to unseen digit counts fails in all formats tested

method.summary: Train NanoGPT (10.6M) and GPT-2 (85M) from random initialization with next-token loss on synthetic arithmetic (add, subtract, multiply, sine, sqrt) in four formats (plain, reverse, simplified scratchpad, detailed scratchpad), varying train-set size, sampling, text mixing and prompting; also fine-tune pretrained GPT-2 and GPT-3 (Ada, Curie, Davinci) on 1,000 examples.
method.task: learning integer arithmetic and elementary functions by next-token prediction

datasets.name: Synthetic 3-digit addition (balanced)
datasets.size: 10,000 samples: all 100 1-digit, 900 2-digit, 9,000 3-digit; about 2,500 each with 0/1/2/3 carries
datasets.split: test: 10,000 uniformly sampled additions not in train
datasets.preprocessing: Smaller sets: all 100 1-digit plus proportionate 2-digit, rest 3-digit (e.g. 450 two-digit at 5,000). Larger sets (20k, 40k) add examples with rejection sampling for carries. Plain format has no zero padding except in the Fig 3 sampling study; reverse adds '$' delimiters.

datasets.name: Synthetic subtraction, multiplication, sine, square root
datasets.size: subtraction: same operand pairs as addition; multiplication: all 100 1x1 cases plus random up to 2-digit (3,000 train in joint run); sine and sqrt: 10,000 each in joint run
datasets.split: test: 10,000 points (7,000 for multiplication) not in train
datasets.source: generated by the authors; sine on [-pi/2, pi/2] and sqrt on [1,10], truncated to 4 decimals
datasets.preprocessing: Reverse multiplication prints the 4-digit product reversed (e.g. '$5 *32= 061$' for 160); reverse subtraction puts the sign last (e.g. '$226 -598= 273-$'); detailed scratchpad for multiplication does 2-digit x 1-digit steps with a power-of-10 shift k; sqrt Newton starts at x_0 = floor of the root; sine Taylor scratchpad has 4 terms (x_1..x_4). (Appendix D.2-D.5)

datasets.name: Shakespeare (char-rnn)
datasets.size: 1,115,394 characters (text says 1,115,394 tokens in Sec 9), 40,000 lines; 64 unique characters
datasets.preprocessing: segmented into dialogue chunks with a random number of addition samples inserted between them; vocabulary of 80 characters for mixed runs

datasets.name: Longer-digit addition (5, 7, 10 digits)
datasets.size: N samples, with d = floor((N-100)/(D(D+1)/2-1)) per digit-length pair (k1<=k2), all 100 1-digit additions first

training.objective: next-token prediction (cross-entropy); GPT-3 via supervised fine-tuning on completions only
training.optimizer: AdamW, betas (0.9, 0.99); GPT-2 mixed-text run betas (0.9, 0.95)
training.lr: NanoGPT 0.001; GPT-2 arithmetic 0.0005; GPT-2 with Shakespeare 0.0006; 4-digit fine-tune study 1e-4 plain, 5e-6 reverse, 1e-5 simple, 1e-6 detailed
training.warmup: NanoGPT plain/reverse 100 iterations, scratchpad 0; GPT-2 plain/reverse 100, scratchpad 0; GPT-2 Shakespeare mix 2000
training.batch_size: NanoGPT plain/reverse 256, scratchpad 16, Shakespeare mix 16; GPT-2 64 (batch 8 with gradient accumulation), Shakespeare mix 40
training.steps: NanoGPT plain/reverse 5,000 iterations, scratchpad 50,000, Shakespeare mix 5,000; GPT-2 plain/reverse 5,000, scratchpad 20,000, Shakespeare mix 50,000
training.seq_len: NanoGPT context 256 (plain/reverse) or 1024 (scratchpad); mean example length 13/15/64/281 tokens for plain/reverse/simplified/detailed

other.few_shot_runs: 1/2/3-shot results averaged over a fixed set of five exemplar sets; text prompts average 25 exemplars

inference.decoding: sampling at temperature 0.8 (stated for all results)
inference.samples: one generation per test item; 10,000 test items (1,000 for GPT-3); few-shot averaged over five fixed exemplar sets
inference.prompting: zero-shot, 1/2/3-shot with same-task or other-task exemplars, text prompts, noisy prompts (wrong sums)

limits: Authors concede no instance of length generalization was observed in any format; they cite Nye et al. 2021 for generalization only above 10^8 parameters.
Authors state it is uncertain whether findings carry to the scale of current LLMs; BPE and larger-model results are preliminary.
Only elementary arithmetic studied: integers up to 3 digits (10 in one study), 2-digit multiplication, 4-decimal sine and sqrt.
No seeds, repeats or confidence intervals reported for accuracy curves, so a single run may drive the phase-transition locations.
GPT-3 fine-tuning used only 1,000 examples for 4 epochs due to budget, with completion-only loss, so it is not comparable to NanoGPT runs.
Sine and sqrt scratchpads involve exponentiation or division no easier than the target, so they gave limited gains.
The PDF is arXiv v1 marked 'Preprint. Under review.' with no venue; the ICLR 2024 venue cited elsewhere is not in this document.
